drafter.private_reasoning: The draft is simple, but the following points warrant advancing for our client: (a) the consideration period (three years) exceeds the proposed agreement term (24 months). We should align protection with the term of the agreement or clarify the relationship. (b) Remedies are briefly stated; our client may benefit from adding that injunctive relief is not the exclusive remedy, and possibly clarifying limitation of liability or specifying no implied license. (c) Add clarity around exclusions from confidential information—a typical NDA carve-out for information that is or becomes public, already possessed, independently developed, or rightfully received from a third party.
drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel:
Dear Counsel,

Thank you for circulating the first draft of the Mutual Non-Disclosure Agreement. Please find attached a mark-up suggesting several clarifications and some additional standard provisions around the term of confidentiality obligations and exclusions from confidential information. We believe these changes will help both parties engage in discussions efficiently and with appropriate protections.

We look forward to your comments.

Best regards,
Aldous Finch LLP

receiver.message_back: Thank you for your suggested clarifications. We are reviewing the proposed survival periods and exclusions, but preliminarily we have concerns regarding both the extended survival of confidentiality obligations and the scope of damages limitations, which we believe should be more narrowly tailored—please confirm your flexibility on these points.

drafter.private_reasoning: Opposing counsel has expressed concerns about both the duration of confidentiality obligations post-termination and the breadth of the damages limitation clause. Our client’s preference is to protect confidentiality for as long as practicable, but we can be somewhat flexible for a compromise. The three-year survival period from the date of disclosure is already a moderate position. On limitation of damages, the current draft excludes all indirect, incidental, or consequential damages, which is favorable but may be narrowed for agreement. To move toward consensus, I propose limiting the exclusion to only consequential damages (removing indirect/incidental), which is customary and addresses their concern while maintaining meaningful protection for our client. I will retain the three-year confidentiality survival period but indicate our willingness to discuss a shorter term, e.g., two years from date of disclosure, to demonstrate good faith.
drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel:
Thank you for your feedback and for highlighting your concerns around the duration of confidentiality obligations and damages limitations. We have considered your comments and believe that a three-year survival period for confidentiality (from the date of disclosure) remains reasonable, given the potential sensitivity of the information exchanged. That said, we are amenable to discussing a reduction of this period to two years if your client requires. 

Regarding the limitation of damages, in the interest of reaching a fair compromise, we have revised the relevant provision to limit only consequential damages, rather than all indirect and incidental damages. We trust this addresses your concern about scope while protecting both parties from unforeseeable liabilities.

We look forward to your response and hope this draft moves us closer to final agreement.

receiver.message_back: Thank you for your revised draft. We are prepared to agree to a two-year survival period for confidentiality from the date of disclosure, provided this applies equally to both parties, and request that the damages section exclude liability only for consequential damages—leaving direct and foreseeable indirect damages available—so as not to unduly limit remedies for breach. Subject to these final adjustments, we are ready to proceed.
